notice.title: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
notice.aiSummary: Lenders using third-party AI models in consumer credit decisions must maintain an inventory of those models and have their model risk committee review each one at least annually for performance and fairness. Compliance is required by June 30, 2027.
notice.aiReason: The notice applies to lenders using third-party AI models for consumer credit decisions, and Brivanta Bank offers multiple credit products where such models could be used for approval, decline, or pricing decisions.

text:
PRUDENTIAL BANKING BOARD FICTIONAL REGULATOR - SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE
Guidance: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
Notice number: RCN-2026-011
Issued by: Prudential Banking Board
Published: 2026-10-09
Effective date: 2027-06-30
1. Who this applies to
Lenders that use models or AI services supplied by third parties to approve, decline or price consumer credit.
2. Background
Lenders are adopting scoring and decision models supplied by vendors, including machine learning and generative AI services. Lenders remain accountable for these models even when they did not build them.
3. Requirements
3.1 A firm must maintain an inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions, recording the supplier, purpose and the products affected.
3.2 The model risk committee must review each third-party AI model in the inventory at least once a year, including its performance and fairness results.
4. Status
Firms must comply with the requirements in section 3 from 2027-06-30.

obligations.noticeTitle: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
obligations.text: A firm must maintain an inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions, recording the supplier, purpose and the products affected.
obligations.controlDesc: Monthly performance monitoring report for internally built credit scorecards
obligations.reason: The obligation requires maintaining an inventory specifically of third-party AI models with supplier, purpose and affected products, but POL-TPR-01 only maintains a general supplier register with criticality ratings and POL-MRM-01 addresses only internally built models, neither capturing the required inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions.

obligations.noticeTitle: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
obligations.text: The model risk committee must review each third-party AI model in the inventory at least once a year, including its performance and fairness results.
obligations.controlDesc: Quarterly capital forecast reviewed by the Board Risk Committee
obligations.reason: The obligation requires review of "each third-party AI model in the inventory" at least annually, but POL-MRM-01 only covers models "built by the bank" and POL-TPR-01 reviews "suppliers that support important business services" without specifically covering third-party AI models or their performance and fairness results.
